messages:
support-sally: :rotating_light: escalated from acct — customer 'MaplePay' is reporting huge latency spikes (2000-3000ms) and intermittent 403s after an automated failover. They say the requests should stay in eu-west but traces show calls going to us-west. Tried to repro, can share traces and headers.

alex-ops: What kind of failover happened? region failover or dedicated pool migration?

support-sally: They had scheduled maintenance on eu-west, traffic failed over to fallback pool. Expected fallback->eu-west-priority, but traffic is landing in us-west. They claim Auth tokens still valid for eu region.

maria-ingest: Can you paste a raw request/response (headers) from the trace? especially X-Region, X-Forwarded-For, and any x-redwood-route headers.

support-sally: Paste from trace (sanitized):
```
> request -> POST /v1/generate
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
> x-client-region: eu-west
> x-request-id: 01F8G2...

< Response 403
< x-upstream-region: us-west
< x-envoy-original-dst-host: vip-10-5-3
< x-redwood-route: pool:d-legacy-us-west
```

kevin-runtime: That x-envoy-original-dst-host and x-redwood-route combo is suspicious — looks like VIP was swapped and L7 route rewrote the route header. Did the gateway do a host rewrite on failover?

alex-ops: I saw an earlier deploy that touched L7 routing rules (PR #5123) which changed fallback ordering for unnamed pools. Could be related. If the gateway is matching on Host header and picking the closest VIP, it might rewrite x-redwood-route to the new pool.

infra-bot: Incident #INC-2026-03-12 created by support-sally for MaplePay — labels: routing, region-failover, envoy.

maria-ingest: Quick repro steps I used locally:
1) curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.example" -H "x-client-region: eu-west" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://gateway.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
2) Observe Response headers for x-upstream-region / x-redwood-route

Curl output snippet I got:
```
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-upstream-region: us-west
< x-redwood-route: pool:d-legacy-us-west
```

kevin-runtime: If the auth check happens at the pool level and the pool expects eu-west tokens, hitting us-west will 403. Two hypotheses: a) VIP mapping table was partially updated so some VIPs point to us-west pools, b) Envoy route/host rewrite is incorrectly normalizing Host -> pool selection on failover.

alex-ops: To rule out VIP mapping we need the VIP -> pool config snapshot from the time of failover. @kevin-runtime can you pull the envoy CDS/EDS snapshot for gateway instances in eu-west at 1798497600 (approx failover time)?

kevin-runtime: Pulling now. Also check if the fallback policy uses region tag or only pool weight; previous config used region affinity but PR #5123 made it weight-only. If weights were equal, the gateway might pick a non-eu pool.

support-sally: Customer is blocked — can we put a temporary mitigation? Maybe force sticky routing by x-client-region header at LB.

maria-ingest: Short-term mitigation: add a header-based route rule that pins requests with x-client-region=eu-west to the eu pools, then roll it to stable. I can push a conservative rule to the eu-west gateway node group.

alex-ops: Do that but keep it narrow (only MaplePay IPs) so it's minimal blast radius. Also capture full capture pcap or tcpdump for one affected connection.

kevin-runtime: Created a targeted header route for MaplePay IPs on eu-west gateway nodes. Pushed change to canary hosts. Monitoring request latency and x-redwood-route on canary: now showing eu-west pool and 120-180ms latency.

support-sally: Customer confirmed improvement on canary, will schedule lift to all nodes after we confirm stability.

maria-ingest: Postmortem notes to investigate: revert PR #5123 or add region-tag to fallback decision, ensure VIP mapping changes are atomic, add test for host header rewrite edge cases, add e2e that simulates scheduled maintenance and verifies region affinity preserved.

alex-ops: Agree. Assigning follow-ups: kevin-runtime (CDS/EDS audit + revert plan), maria-ingest (route rule QA + e2e), support-sally (customer comms + billing hold if needed).

infra-bot: Follow-up checklist created: [CDS audit, PR revert, e2e, canary validation].
